Key architecture findings:

- `freshness_state` (P35.33) already implements the K9 §5.1 truth table +
  `evaluated_at` + `run_record_missing` — the ticket's `freshness_verdict`
  is the same function under the contract name, one implementation.
- The transparency emit already receives a release-bound `at`
  (`dataset.as_of → generated_at → now`, `spine_export.py:4042`) — the
  release-side of the two-clocks rule stands; the status lane is P36.43's.
- `_source_volatility` already votes over all claims passed (dated and
  undated alike); the remaining gap is the dominant-class+half-life
  emission and the interim basis label.
- `_last_upstream_change` compares capture byte digests — the direct
  SIG-TRANSP-031 gap (a formatting-only byte change may move the date).
- `claim_set_fingerprint` (P35.22) IS the canonical
  volatile-field-free sha256 over sorted records — `records_digest`
  reuses it verbatim at the flush seam.
- `FetchResult.headers` carries the response headers (S-14 scrub at the
  transparency boundary); the metadata GET is one bounded read per
  platform metadata URL per run through `ctx.fetcher` (the shared
  politeness layer — robots, rate limits and per_fetch telemetry bind
  it like any egress).
- `ingest_run_capture` PK is `(run_id, target_key, state)` — the new
  fields land as nullable additive columns; `v_transparency_capture`
  gains them via `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` in one new sqitch change.
- `ops/alerts.py` is the recorded-alert ledger; no freshness evaluation
  exists ops-side yet — the shared function plus one shared
  verdict→issue-class mapping is what exporter and ACT-02 consume.

## Phase 2 — implementation notes

Shared verdict (SIG-TRANSP-029):
- `policy/src/policy/freshness.py` — `freshness_verdict(cadence…, executions, at)`
  is the one pure function: closed state set, `run_record_missing`,
  `evaluated_at` on every verdict, `next_scheduled_day` only when the
  caller asks (`include_next_fire=True` — status lane only).
  `freshness_state`/`FreshnessState` kept as delegating aliases — one
  implementation, never a dual run. `freshness_issue_class` is the one
  verdict→issue mapping exporter and ACT-02 share.
- `exports/transparency.py freshness_records` calls `freshness_verdict`
  at the release `at` (spine_export derives it `dataset.as_of →
  generated_at → now`, `spine_export.py:4042`).
- `build_spine_export`/`run_spine_export` now take
  `cadence_sources`/`scheduler_drift` pass-throughs (default `_UNSET` →
  the emit loads committed `ops/cadence.toml`; explicit `None` stays the
  honest "doc unreadable" marker — the pre-change default would have
  labelled every row `not_recorded`).

Volatility + staleness (SIG-TRANSP-030, K9 §5.2–5.3):
- Two new `TRANSPARENCY_QUERIES` reads: `freshness_predicates`
  (per-(source,predicate) claim + dated counts over ALL publishable-
  eligible claims) and `freshness_observations` (deduped latest dated obs
  per (source,subject,predicate)) — the K-3 dated/site-only bias is dead.
  Pre-P35.41 raw maps / guard misses degrade to the same aggregates over
  the caller's claims — honestly narrower, never a widened read.
- `_source_volatility` emits `distribution`, `dominant {class,
  half_life_days}` (most-claimed registry class, deterministic), and
  `unregistered_predicate` — claims on predicates the registry does not
  declare are counted, never silently dropped.
- `_source_staleness` ages each deduped latest dated observation against
  its predicate half-life at `at` → `evaluable`/`stale`/`dated_unevaluable`.
  The row emits `stale n` only when evaluable > 0 — an unevaluable source
  carries `evaluable`/`not_evaluable` counts, never "0 stale", never
  "unknown".
- `shaping.py`: new `freshness_predicates` shaping read;
  `ShapedSourceFreshness` gains `evaluated_at` (the release as-of),
  `staleness_evaluable_count` (the m), `undated_count`,
  `volatility_distribution`, `unregistered_predicate_count`; the P35.20b
  declared-class staleness gate is unchanged (a declared-class verdict is
  never replaced by a vote).
- `web/metrics.ts FreshnessRow` + `assertFreshnessRow` require the five
  new fields; the data-freshness page renders "stale n of m evaluable",
  "+ m undated", and the `evaluated_at` disclosure (release clock named
  vs reader clock). Fixture rows carry the fields.

Two change dates (SIG-TRANSP-031, K9 §5.4):
- `_last_upstream_change`: newest upstream-DECLARED instant across marks
  (basis names the declared field) → else `records_digest` diff on flushed
  marks (byte-only changes never move it) → else `not_detectable` (incl.
  token-only publishers — an ETag declares a version, never a date; no
  retrieval-clock substitution ever).
- `_last_sig_records_change`: `records_digest` diff when comparable, else
  J3's labelled interim "last run that added claims — not a content-change
  measure", else `first_release`/`not_published` tokens (P36.68's
  release-slice diff lands beside it, named).
- `capture_record` emits `records_digest` + `upstream_declared
  {modified_at, token, basis}`; `order_capture_records` diffs
  `records_digest` when comparable — a byte diff alone marks
  `formatting change only`.

Connector capture side:
- `connectors/upstream_modified.py` (new): `upstream_declared(target,
  fetched, fetcher, metadata_cache)` — metadata GET (ArcGIS `?f=json`
  `editingInfo.lastEditDate`, Socrata `/api/views/<id>.json`
  `rowsUpdatedAt`/`dataUpdatedAt`, CKAN `metadata_url`
  `metadata_modified`), then payload-declared (EoF
  `portals[].data_last_updated`), then S-14 headers (`Last-Modified`,
  `ETag`). Probe failures degrade to honest absence, never run-fatal;
  one metadata GET per metadata URL per run (cache-deduped); the probe
  rides `ctx.fetcher` (robots/rate-limit/opt-out/per_fetch telemetry).
- `CaptureRef` gains `upstream_modified_at`/`upstream_token`/
  `upstream_modified_basis` (declared metadata, never part of the content
  address). `CaptureLedger.record_capture` + `PgClaimSink.record_capture`
  carry them + `records_digest` (flushed marks only).
- `pipeline._emit` computes `records_digest =
  claim_set_fingerprint(claims, classes=predicate_temporal_classes())` —
  the volatile-field-free fingerprint — and the flushed mark carries it;
  `_mark_capture`/`_capture_of` round-trip the declared triple so a
  resumed capture keeps its acquisition's declaration.
- `FetchResult.headers` forwarded through `procurement._merge_pages` (the
  declared lane survives a merged multi-page capture).
- `FetchRecord` gains run-level `records_digest` (order-independent
  fingerprint over per-capture digests) + `capture_upstream[]`.
- New sqitch `capture_freshness_marks`: `ingest_run_capture` +
  `records_digest`/`upstream_modified_at`/`upstream_token`/
  `upstream_modified_basis`, CHECK `records_digest IS NULL OR
  state='flushed'`, `v_transparency_capture` gains all four appended;
  NULL-tolerant — no backfill invents a declared value.
  `_RESUME_MARKS`/`_RECORD_CAPTURE` carry the columns with a legacy-shape
  fallback on `UndefinedColumn` (a spine one migration behind still
  records marks).

Tests added: `tests/connectors/test_p35_41_upstream_declared.py` (18),
`tests/exports/test_p35_41_freshness.py` (17),
`tests/db/test_resume_pg.py::test_freshness_columns_round_trip_and_check`
(real-PG round-trip + CHECK refusal), verdict-contract cases in
`tests/unit/test_policy_freshness.py` (26 total).

Status lane / ACT-02: no ops-side freshness evaluation exists yet (the
status lane is P36.43's); `freshness_verdict` + `freshness_issue_class`
are the single implementations those lanes call — there is no second
semantics to converge.

## Phase 3 — self-review

Two passes over the diff (mechanical + design), 2026-10-20:

Mechanical pass — defects found and fixed in-flight:
- `_source_staleness` subtracted a tz-aware `_dt()` observed_at from a
  possibly-naive release `at` — `TypeError` on real PG
  (`test_spine_export_over_seeded_spine` ×4). Fixed: `eval_at` normalises
  `at` to UTC-aware inside the function only (the emitted `evaluated_at`
  keeps the caller's own format). `freshness_verdict` already normalises
  both sides internally (policy/freshness.py:426,453).
- The issue emitter hard-coded `state in {"late","overdue","never_run"}`
  — a second verdict→issue mapping next to `freshness_issue_class` (the
  dual-run shape the ticket forbids). Fixed: the emitter consults the one
  shared mapping (transparency.py:2305).
- `test_transparency_view_columns` pinned the ORIGINAL
  `transparency_views.sql` view shape against the evolved allow-list —
  append-only sqitch discipline puts the current shape in the newest
  `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` (`capture_freshness_marks`). Fixed the test,
  not the invariant: it now resolves the LAST deploy definition +
  LAST verify `WHERE FALSE` select per view in `sqitch.plan` order —
  a stronger closure (deploy∪verify∪allow-list on the landed shape,
  and it accepts `CREATE OR REPLACE`).
- `db/sqitch.plan`'s new `planned_at` (2026-10-20T21:19:34Z, real
  `date -u`) is future-of-HEAD (62601e55 @ 20:57Z) → the whole-tree
  date guard flagged it. Fixed per the documented mechanism (c): an
  expiring `allow` entry in `docs/build/tools/record_policy/history.policy`
  (convention verbatim from the P35.x rows above it).
- `docs/build/runs/P35.41.md`'s run-ledger leg-record cell hit the
  assert lint (the `live` token with no negate in-segment). Reworded —
  the cell now reads the honest posture (pre-authorised; deferred under
  OM-19 — the AR-3 slot had passed and the session digest records a
  dispatch hold).

Design pass — confirmed, no defects:
- `upstream_declared`'s probe rides `ctx.fetcher` (PoliteFetcher): the
  metadata GET inherits robots/opt-out/rate-limit/per-fetch telemetry;
  `api_allow_reason` classifies it API-mode where allow-listed. A refusal
  or parse failure degrades to honest absence — never run-fatal.
  Deduped per metadata URL per run; skipped entirely on non-mark-writing
  runs (`declared_fetcher = ctx.fetcher if ledger is not None else None`).
- `CaptureRef.upstream_*` is declared metadata, never part of the content
  address (`canonical()` unchanged). Resume round-trips the declared
  value via `_capture_of`; a reprocessed capture's flushed mark carries a
  fresh `records_digest` of what THAT run emitted.
- `PgClaimSink.record_capture` falls back to the legacy INSERT inside a
  savepoint ONLY on `UndefinedColumn` — CHECK violations and constraint
  failures still propagate (the schema-compat escape never swallows a
  real refusal). `records_digest` on a `captured` mark is refused by the
  new CHECK (verified on real PG).
- `_RESUME_MARKS` catches `UndefinedColumn` like `UndefinedTable`: a
  spine one migration behind runs without resume (slower, correct —
  re-fetch dedupes by content identity) rather than failing.
- `procurement._merge_pages` forwards `first.headers` so the header lane
  survives merged multi-page captures.
- The shaped `status` (ok/failing/retired/degraded/not_evaluable) is the
  run-status disclosure, intentionally distinct from the cadence verdict —
  both honestly labelled; `inference.SourceFreshness.__post_init__`
  still refuses a nonzero stale count on a non-evaluable row.
- `ops/alerts.py` contains no freshness evaluation (notifier/ledger
  seam only); `api/store_pg.sources_with_freshness` carries the shaped
  fields verbatim. `freshness_verdict` + `freshness_issue_class` are the
  single implementations the status lane (P36.43) and ACT-02 consume —
  nothing else to converge.
